summary: Round-2 re-validation: all round-1 fixes applied cleanly, no new structural issues. Task 1 description trimmed to 4 sentences (within the 5-sentence ceiling) with a single trailing 'See Decisions 1-8 for rationale' pointer; Architecture > Shared resources replaced with 'None' plus a one-line note explaining why (no DB pool, no LLM client, no browser). Task numbering left as-is per operator decision (cosmetic, never blocking). New content reviewed: Decision 8 (security hardening) follows the Decision/Rationale/Alternatives format, is marked [TECHNICAL], and is mirrored in User-Spec Deviations; the inline ES1-ES10 error matrix lives inside Architecture > How it works as a table (no template violation, improves readability); 8 new Security ACs are concrete and testable; Risks table gained a 6th row covering adversarial input that aligns with Decision 8. Frontmatter still valid (created 2026-04-25, status draft, branch dev, size S). All required sections present and non-empty. Skills (code-writing, code-reviewing, security-auditor, test-master, pre-deploy-qa) and reviewers (code-reviewer, security-auditor, test-reviewer for Task 1; none for Audit Wave and Final Wave) match the canonical catalog; reviewer agent files exist on disk. Wave conflict check: Wave 1 has a single modifying task; Audit Wave and Final Wave are read-only. No time-based estimates anywhere. Task brevity check: all five task descriptions are 3-4 sentences; no Acceptance Criteria or TDD Anchor sections inside tasks; no line-number references in any task description (line numbers in Files to read are context pointers, not implementation steps); no decision rationale embedded in task descriptions (Task 1 uses a single closing reference; Task 2 lists audit verification items, which is appropriate for a code-audit task). Zero critical, zero major, zero minor findings - status is approved and the spec is ready for decomposition.
